conventions.convention: L is an integer at least 3; all coordinate indices are modulo L. There are L² vertices, 2L² edge qubits, and L² faces. Chains and support relations use F₂ coefficients.
Stars use X on incident edges; plaquettes use Z on face boundaries. Edge factors are ordered lexicographically by (i,j), horizontal before vertical at each coordinate.
An e defect is a negative star eigenvalue; an m defect is a negative plaquette eigenvalue. These are finite check-syndrome labels without a material-quasiparticle assumption.
The Hamiltonian is −J_e times the star sum minus J_m times the plaquette sum, with J_e,J_m strictly positive; each violated check costs twice its coupling.
Z₁ uses h_{i,0}, Z₂ uses v_{0,j}, X₁ uses h_{0,j}, and X₂ uses v_{i,0}; equal-index X/Z pairs cross once.
Disk indistinguishability requires a compact embedded disk with connected complement containing both the complete primal edge segment and its crossing dual segment for every supported qubit.

An elementary Pauli path starts at I, multiplies by one-edge X, Y, or Z at each step, and ends at a scalar-phase multiple of the specified logical representative. Its barrier minimizes the peak energy excess over such paths.
Recovery uses an integer t ≥ 0 with the strict inequality 2t < L and finite channels whose Kraus operators lie in the span of weight-at-most-t Paulis.

load_bearing.statement: For the periodic L×L toric checks with L≥3, the common +1 eigenspace is a valid stabilizer code on n=2L² qubits. Its independent check rank is r=2L²−2, so its dimension is 4 and it encodes two logical qubits.

For L≥3, the L² star-support vectors have span dimension L²−1 and their only relation is their total sum. The face-boundary vectors have the same span dimension and sole total-sum relation. The dual-face incidence statement has the same rank.

For primal cycles Z₁ and the span B₁ of face boundaries, B₁⊆Z₁, Z₁/B₁ has dimension two, and the two winding parities give coordinates on that quotient; the statement also asserts the corresponding dual quotient.
All star and plaquette checks commute. The product of all stars is the identity, and the product of all plaquettes is the identity.

An edge-simple primal Z trail with distinct endpoints has syndrome exactly at its two endpoint stars; an edge-simple dual X trail has syndrome exactly at its two endpoint plaquettes. Closed trails of either kind have zero syndrome.
For J_e,J_m>0, the ground space is the four-dimensional toric code space, E_g=−L²(J_e+J_m), and the exact spectral gap above it is Δ_L=4 min(J_e,J_m).
For the periodic L×L toric stabilizer code with L≥3, the minimum weight of a normalizer Pauli outside the scalar-phase stabilizer is d(S)=L.

In the infinite square lattice, every finitely supported edge chain over F₂ whose incidence at each vertex is even is the boundary of a finitely supported collection of square faces. The same conclusion holds for the translated dual square lattice.

A nonempty compact embedded topological disk D⊆T_L with connected complement has a lift on which the quotient map is one-to-one and maps homeomorphically onto D; finite primal and dual chains supported in D lift, and cycles lift to cycles.

concerns.concern: Proof step 2.1 says, “These endpoints define a section $\widetilde D\to\mathbb R^2$ of $\pi$ over $D$.” The constructed endpoint assignment has domain D; its image is the lifted disk subsequently denoted by the tilde. The displayed domain is a notation error in an otherwise sound lifting argument.

The Statement says the dual assertion uses “dual vertex boundaries in place of face boundaries.” Boundaries spanning the dual cycle subspace are dual face boundaries, corresponding to stars around primal vertices. Steps 2.1–3.1 use the correct square-cellulation argument, but the stated terminology does not identify that subspace correctly.
